title: Present continuous
tagline: Now vs always — and the verbs that never take -ing.
exam: Listening Part 1 — a picture and five short conversations
Reading Part 6 — a text describing what people are doing
why: The present continuous doesn't just mean 'now' — it also means 'around now', for a temporary situation that isn't finished. The real challenge at A2 is choosing between present simple and present continuous, and knowing that verbs like know, want and understand almost never take -ing. Get this contrast right and your English sounds natural, not just correct.

hook.text: Saturday morning at the market. "Look, Mateo is buying mangoes right now," says Sofia. "He usually buys apples, but today he's trying something new. I know he loves fruit!"
hook.ask: Find one verb that describes what's happening right now, one that describes a routine, and one state verb that never takes -ing. Which is which?

diagrams.title: Now, routine, or a feeling?
diagrams.caption: Continuous = happening now / temporary. Simple = routine / always true. State verbs (know, like, want) stay simple.

rows.label: Time words
cells: now, at the moment, today, look!

diagrams.title: Spelling the -ing form

rules.rule: one vowel + one consonant: double the consonant
verb ending in -e: drop the e + ing

diagrams.caption: buy and try keep the y — only verbs ending in a consonant + y change it, and only for -s, not -ing.

use.point: Right now / at the moment — present continuous

examples.text: We're waiting for the bus at the moment.
It's raining, so we're staying inside.
The market opens at seven every day.
I go to the market every Saturday, but today I'm going with my mum.
She plays tennis on Tuesdays, but right now she's doing her homework.
examples.note: usual habit vs this exact moment

examples.text: I know this stall — it's the best one.
examples.note: know describes a fact in your head, not an action

examples.text: Sofia likes mangoes, and she wants two kilos.
examples.note: like and want are feelings, so they stay simple

examples.text: Do you understand the price in soles?
examples.note: understand is a state, never understanding

watch_out.why: know is a state verb — it doesn't take -ing.
want describes a feeling, so it stays in the present simple.
right now needs the present continuous, not the present simple.
every Tuesday is a routine, so use the present simple.
buy keeps the y before -ing: buying, not buing.
understand is a state verb, even with now.

l1.why: In Spanish saber can sound like an action, but in English know is a state verb and stays simple.
want is a feeling, so it never takes -ing.

l1.es: Voy al mercado todos los sábados.
l1.wrong: I'm going to the market every Saturday.
l1.right: I go to the market every Saturday.
l1.why: every Saturday is a routine, so it needs the present simple, not the continuous.
right now needs the present continuous, not the simple.
understand describes knowledge in your head, not an action — it stays simple.

remember.tip: Ask yourself: is it happening at this exact second, or is it always true? And never put -ing on know, like, want or understand.

dialogue.title: At the Saturday market
dialogue.context: Sofia and Mateo are at the Saturday market in Lima for a class project on Peruvian food.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Look, Mateo! You're trying a new stall today.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Yes! I usually buy apples, but this mango looks amazing.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: I know that stall — it's the best one in the market.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Not yet. I want some bread, but the bakery is closing soon.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Quick then! What time does the market usually close?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: At one o'clock. Right now it's only eleven, so we're fine!

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Great. Let's go before it gets too busy.

items.why: look! signals something happening right now.
every Saturday signals a routine, so use the present simple.

items.sentence: I ___ the answer — don't tell me!
items.why: know is a state verb and never takes -ing.

items.sentence: She ___ a new bike at the moment — she's saving money.
items.why: want is a state verb, so it stays simple even with at the moment.
understand is a state verb, so the question uses do.

items.sentence: Right now, we ___ for the bus.
items.why: right now signals the present continuous.
buy keeps the y before -ing: buying.

items.sentence: The market ___ at one o'clock every day.
items.why: every day signals the present simple, and the market (it) takes -s.

can_do: I can use the present continuous for now and the present simple for routines, and choose the right one.
I can spell the -ing form correctly, including tricky verbs like buy and sit.
I can use state verbs like know, like, want and understand in the present simple, never with -ing.
summary: Present continuous = am/is/are + verb-ing, for now or a temporary situation.
Present simple = routines and facts — every day, usually, always.
Spelling: sit → sitting, make → making, buy → buying.
State verbs — know, like, want, understand — almost never take -ing, even with now.
Ask: happening at this second, or always true? That tells you which tense to use.
